approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a population of genuinely scored molecules. It fits a task-local Gaussian process to raw count fingerprints and accepted scores, generates a fresh pool through crossover and mutation, and draws one coherent function for each purchase. Each function guides eight rounds of bounded graph edits from a four-molecule beam. Its values stay cached as the path grows. After every path finishes, the Parent buys distinct available sampled maxima in path order and uses only their real scores for subsequent fitting, survival and breeding. It measures real stalls but currently leaves those final path purchases unrestricted.
approach.novelty: Add a mean screen only to the completed paths at purchase time. Once the inherited counter reaches three non-improving batches, each path may buy from its forty highest real-GP means, while still choosing by its original cached sampled function. The hypothesis is that this support restriction prevents weakly supported optimistic maxima from consuming scarce evaluations and improves realized gain over the scored generating roots. This Parent has no same-Parent siblings. Earlier screen evidence concerns a fixed generated pool; applying the same eligibility principle after coherent graph expansion is the new applicability case. Exploration itself remains the Parent algorithm.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-eb15da16dbea successfully optimized coherent posterior paths but paid for sampled maxima that yielded too little real improvement over their scored generating roots. All 4350 purchases and 34800 expansion waves completed; 3584 purchases were absent from their base pools and 2403 were deeper than one extension, yet complete equal-session positive generating-root gain fell to 0.0030352346989319977 from 0.0038830439945360625, and the endpoint mean was 0.5647856486588217 versus the formal Anchor/code ancestor 0.607030316211131. Its mechanism_result=refuted and triggered useful-extension falsifier remain immutable. The frozen Search audit, independently reproduced read-only for all 15 sessions in policy/scratch/r0076-01-improve-L01/plan/evidence-review.json, identifies the bounded obstacle: among 1330 stalled actual purchases, 733 were certainly outside their own visited top40 real-GP means. Their mean positive root gain was 0.0002968452481569561 and realized-minus-sampled residual -0.16912108902862596, versus 0.002245126526717109 and -0.13423038332446488 in the 597 inside purchases; no boundary tie occurred. These are selected observational groups, not counterfactual outcomes. The exact eligibility-consumer control n-c501ea219a1c on n-cf8d309c06de supplies contextual evidence that the original screen can change paid feedback and have positive retained total contribution on the original finite-pool host. Its result does not establish screen value after coherent graph expansion.

adoptions.applicability: n-eb15da16dbea is a complete exposed refutation of useful unguarded extension: exact coherent conditioning passed, 3584 products were outside the seed pool and 2403 were deeper than one extension, yet full/late positive root gain and all seed endpoints declined (mean delta -0.042244667552309344). The immutable result is not repaired. In all 1330 stalled actual purchases, a passive per-path mean rank audit finds 733 certainly outside top40 with markedly lower root gain and more negative sampled residual than the 597 inside; all labels are actual purchases and no mean-boundary tie occurred. This is support for a new support-screen experiment, not a causal estimate or transported screen benefit. The complete Parent already logged every visited real-GP mean alongside exact sampled values and completed4350 paths/34800 waves; the screen needs sorting only, no posterior evaluation beyond what ran. Its measured entire replica wall sum3311.5659922900377s, RSS1094676KiB and CUDA43122688bytes leave a bounded local arithmetic operation plausible under the unchanged7200s per-task limit. Each path has160 base identities, so retaining40 before at most9 preceding purchases preserves batch feasibility. Whole-job GPU peaks are not measured; verify exact construction and resource use.

hypothesis: Mean-screened coherent path purchase. Leave all base generation, exact latent paths, eight expansion waves, top-four beams, graph admissions and path random streams unchanged. Only final purchase eligibility changes: if the inherited real stall streak is at least three, rank each path complete visited feasible identities by its unchanged real-GP mean with canonical-identity tie breaking, retain the highest min(40,N), then select its highest cached function value still available in original path order. Compute the screen before excluding earlier batch purchases, as in the original eligibility consumer; with ten paths and at least160 base identities the screen cannot exhaust from nine prior choices. Nonstalled purchases remain unguarded. Do not gate expansion, resample a path, refit a predictor, change residual scale, or convert virtual values to labels.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-screened purchases improved root gain and code-Parent scores, while remaining below the formal Anchor
finding_summary.insights:
This result establishes that the final mean eligibility screen can improve useful paid feedback on an expanded coherent-path search, beyond merely changing ranks or lowering sampled optimism. It leaves the earlier unguarded-extension refutation intact. The conditional positive total effect belongs to this one screen on this measured host; the experiment does not separately establish the value of coherent expansion, the GP, its residual, or the graph operators, and passive alternatives have no counterfactual rewards. The retained finite Gaussian sampling element operated as specified; the screen remains an internal adaptation rather than a performance claim imported from the source paper.

The remaining limitation is productive search, not path consistency or execution cost. Even after screening, 3,804 of 4,350 purchases did not beat their real roots; 3,081 nonterminal purchases never appeared as generating roots of a later accepted purchase. Purchased sampled values still exceeded realized scores by 0.141 on average. The GP mean ordered 68.4% of untied co-purchased pairs correctly, versus 71.7% in the Parent, so reduced sampled optimism did not establish a better calibrated ranking model. The chemistry report finds broad exploration but concentration of some upper-score bands in few core structures, alongside destructive contractions, oversized graphs and mixed changes in unusual heteroatom bonds. These observations identify two unresolved method limitations: ranking proposed improvements by their likely real usefulness, and generating structurally coherent alternatives to locally favored cores. A different predictive ranking model or context-sensitive graph proposal/search scheme could address those limitations; this panel does not establish their benefit. Neither smaller molecules nor this screen's local gain establishes formal-Anchor recovery or a verdict on the whole approach.
finding_summary.results: The screen operated correctly on the complete three-seed panel. It changed 487 of 940 stalled purchases across 94 announcements; all 3,410 nonstalled purchases retained the unguarded choice on the same available graphs. All 4,350 purchases reached real feedback. Mean positive gain over the actual scored generating roots rose from 0.00303523 to 0.00355162; late gain rose from 0.00150782 to 0.00188030. Root-beating purchases increased from 462 to 546. Full-session gain increased in 14 sessions; the one session that never screened was unchanged. The useful-transfer falsifier therefore did not trigger. Final mean score rose from 0.564786 to 0.578030, a paired gain of 0.013244, with positive macro differences on all three seeds and no material task regression against the code Parent. The separate formal Anchor remains higher at 0.607030: the Child trails it by 0.029000 and has a material sitagliptin regression. The global endpoint criterion also requires the formal Anchor itself as code Parent, which this descendant does not satisfy.

molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry with persistent reactive bond motifs, undefined stereochemistry and concentrated upper-score families
molecular.overall_character: This describes n-dc60d82e4f36 against actual code Parent n-eb15da16dbea. The frozen comparison independently marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete; all fifteen Child and fifteen Parent Search trajectories were present, with no uncovered tasks or missing paired chemistry files. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is a different node and is not substituted for the code Parent; no separate formal-Anchor chemistry comparison is made here. Each task contributes 870 accepted optimizer products, excluding supplied initial records, for 4,350 products per node. These are purchased outputs, not every internally considered graph. The output contains fused and bridged aromatic/alicyclic systems, linked heteroarenes, ordinary amides and amines, cyclic carbonyl/imino/thione groups, ethers and extensive halogen substitution. The digest ring-marker rates are 0.9782 to 0.9954 and aromatic-marker rates 0.9471 to 0.9874; these are fractions of strings containing markers, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. RDKit finds aromatic atoms in 4,234 products. Median heavy-atom count is 31 versus Parent 32; the Child spans 1 to 113 heavy atoms. There are 61 products with at most six heavy atoms and 217 with at least fifty, versus Parent 87 and 246. Local chemical compatibility remains uneven. Nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and oxygen-oxygen bonds occur in 999, 656 and 287 Child products versus Parent 1,384, 525 and 320: no uniform improvement across these flags. RDKit also flags 98 products with an all-aromatic perceived ring of at most four atoms versus Parent 77; this is a geometric review cue, not proof of impossibility. There are 3,230 products with unassigned tetrahedral stereocentres and zero with assigned centres, versus Parent 3,175 and zero. Child formal-charge count is zero, versus Parent 86; neutral representation does not imply absence of ionizable amines. The declared nonamide-amine proxy matches 2,091 products, including 1,054 with a matching ring nitrogen. The complete set has 2,265 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,345 generic scaffolds, versus Parent 2,348 and 1,454. Exploration is structurally broad, with conditional concentration in some upper-score families. The synthetic-plausibility and drug-likeness judgments reflect the unusual bonds, ring junctions and size tails, while recognizing that ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs are also present. No synthetic route, conformer stability, pKa or biological activity is established by these trajectories. Pooled task score deciles contain 87 products; per-session deciles contain 29, with initial records excluded. Functional-group counts use the exact published SMARTS; the uppercase-carbon carbonyl/amide queries are not exhaustive counts of aromatic lactam carbonyls. All early and late purchases and both size tails remain in the audits. The score-gradient readings are descriptive associations, not causal edits, hidden-target reconstruction, component attribution or activation judgments. Definitions, exact source files and hashes: policy/scratch/r0076-01-improve-L01/molecular/evidence-manifest.json; counts and score-band summaries: policy/scratch/r0076-01-improve-L01/molecular/descriptor-summary.json.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
